ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Albumin binding

Two otherwise similar drugs differ mainly in plasma albumin binding. Drug A remains strongly bound within plasma, while drug B binds less to albumin and enters tissues more readily. Which distribution pattern is most likely for drug A under these assumptions?

  1. A necessarily larger Vd
  2. No measurable plasma concentration
  3. Distribution only into adipose tissue
  4. A Vd of zero
  5. A smaller apparent volume of distribution
Answer and explanation

A smaller apparent volume of distribution

Greater plasma confinement tends to reduce Vd when other factors are comparable.

Option explanations

A smaller apparent volume of distribution: Greater plasma confinement tends to reduce Vd when other factors are comparable.

A necessarily larger Vd: More plasma confinement does not favor a larger Vd.

No measurable plasma concentration: Plasma-bound drug contributes to total plasma concentration.

Distribution only into adipose tissue: Albumin binding does not imply selective fat distribution.

A Vd of zero: Drug still occupies an apparent plasma distribution space.
